name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,386

clue.text: With generous spirit not present, heartless? I am

definitions.text: With generous spirit not present, heartless? I am

indicators.note: a thing without its heart has lost its middle, so the central letter of the phrase before it goes

blocks.note: a big-hearted person has a generous spirit
someone out is not present

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being mean-spirited and cold-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: BIG plus OUT with its middle U removed gives BIGOT, and the whole clue is the bigot's own confession: no generous spirit, no heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow-minded, intolerant person has neither generosity of spirit nor warmth, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Bishop aroused rising censure with small biscuit

indicators.note: in a down entry something rising is read from the bottom upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
randy means sexually aroused
to censure is to criticise harshly, as a critic pans a show

explanation.surface: A churchman is roused and rebuked over a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: A brandy snap is a thin, rolled, crisp ginger biscuit, popular in Britain and often filled with cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The brandy snap is a little lacy rolled ginger biscuit, so it is an example of a small sweet bake.

clue.text: Novelist who wrote The Rat is a Rat

blocks.note: first meaning: Günter ..., the German author of the novel The Rat
second meaning: an informer, British slang for someone who tells tales to the police

explanation.surface: A literary quip that the author of The Rat is himself a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is British slang for a police informer, which is also what a rat is.
explanation.definitionFit: Günter Grass wrote the novel The Rat, and a grass, like a rat, is someone who betrays others to authorities.

clue.text: Wind swept with hot breath round Eastern establishment

indicators.note: to wind something is to twist and coil it, so the following letters are turned about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A hot desert wind blowing around some eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind swept' looks like a single adjective, windswept, but Wind is the anagram signal and swept is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Establishment means the ruling authorities collectively, the people in charge who hold power over others.

clue.text: Now and then, when I relax, a call for help goes round

indicators.note: something that goes round another encircles it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: me time is a period set aside for one's own relaxation
SOS is the international distress signal

explanation.surface: Someone sometimes hears distress calls while trying to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe something happening occasionally rather than constantly, on some occasions only.

clue.text: After a fashion show's over, Russian tries on Finn's tops

indicators.note: the top of each word in a down entry is its opening letter, so the initials are taken

blocks.clueFragment: show's over, Russian tries on Finn's
blocks.note: initial letters of the six words

explanation.surface: After a fashion show ends, a Russian model tries on a Finnish one's tops.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reuses 'After a fashion' as a pun on a fashion show, so the definition seems to bleed into the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a rough, approximate way is doing it after a fashion, somewhat or to some extent.

clue.text: Supply real item for equipment

indicators.note: supply as an adjective means pliant and bendy, so the letters that follow are flexed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to provide a genuine article for kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as a verb but is the adjective meaning flexible, pronounced 'supply' to rhyme with simply.
explanation.definitionFit: Materiel is military kit and supplies: weapons, vehicles and gear issued to armed forces.

clue.text: Help with problems when hard foreign currency's first invested in area of London

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go within the place

blocks.note: the rouble is Russia's currency
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
Tooting is a district of south London

explanation.surface: Talk of hard currency being invested in a London district sounds like financial news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells you the currency comes ahead of the H before both go inside TOOTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubleshooting is diagnosing and fixing faults, which is assistance given with difficulties or breakdowns.

clue.text: For heaven's sake go away and find something to eat

blocks.note: 'Man!' is an exclamation of exasperation
'get out' means go away

explanation.surface: An exasperated person is told to leave and get some food.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangetout is a flat pea pod eaten whole; the name is French for 'eat all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout peas are a vegetable eaten pod and all, so they are an edible item, a deliberately vague food.

clue.text: Famous crisis when Greek god goes north

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means travelling upwards, so the name is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Zeus is king of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A historical crisis when the king of the gods heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Suez Crisis of 1956 saw Britain and France invade Egypt over the Suez Canal, and fail.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1956 Suez affair is a well-known political and military emergency in British post-war history.

clue.text: Unpaid team at European shows

indicators.note: the phrase shows the word within it, displaying it among its letters

blocks.note: spans the end of team, all of at, and the start of European

explanation.surface: A European sports team proves to be unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part without payment, unlike a professional who is paid for it.

clue.text: Ogre’s followed by kinsman hiding every large hammer

indicators.note: hiding every large means each L, the abbreviation for large, is concealed and dropped from the words

blocks.note: a troll is an ogre-like monster
an uncle is a male relative

explanation.surface: A monster and his relative conceal a big hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ls go: one pair from the troll, one from the uncle, since 'every' covers all three. 'hammer' looks like an object but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce an opponent is to beat them heavily, and to hammer a rival is informal for a crushing defeat.

clue.text: Some food in front of us but no tea, you say? Shameful!

indicators.note: no tells you the item named after it is to be left out
you say means the drink is taken as a sound, the letter it is spoken like

blocks.note: a dish is a serving of food
a meal set on our table is right in front of us
the drink is spoken like the letter that is removed

explanation.surface: A diner complains that there is food but no tea, and calls it a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: DISH ON OUR TABLE loses its T, the letter that sounds like tea, leaving DISHONOURABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonourable behaviour brings disgrace, so it is shameful in the sense of deserving reproach.

clue.text: Poor king, poor king, reflect carefully!

blocks.note: poor can mean meagre or thin
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the phrase repeated says the first one is written two times over

explanation.surface: A lament for a pitiful monarch, followed by advice to take care.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition is itself the wordplay: Poor king is THIN K, and saying it again says that word twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To think twice is to reconsider before acting, which is pondering a decision with care.

clue.text: What follows search for fleece, according to storyteller?

indicators.note: a storyteller speaks the words aloud, so it is their spoken form that counts

blocks.note: to seek is to search, and wool is the fleece of a sheep

explanation.surface: A storyteller recounts the hunt for a fleece, like Jason's quest for the Golden Fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: The Golden Fleece suggests a myth, and a sequel is what a storyteller writes next.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequel is a later work continuing an earlier story, so it is the thing that comes after.

clue.text: Act out of turn with question before EU judge, interrupting EU legislator

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another, so it goes inside

blocks.note: QU is an abbreviation for question
taken as written
J is the abbreviation for judge
EU followed by MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A procedural row in a European court and parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: J goes between the E and the U of EU MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To queue-jump is to push ahead of others waiting, taking a place before one's proper turn.

clue.text: Whether he is an insect or a great beast

blocks.note: the old subjunctive 'be he' means whether he is
a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: A question about whether some creature is small or huge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be he a moth or a beast' is old-fashioned English for 'whether he is a moth or a beast'.
explanation.definitionFit: The behemoth is a huge creature from the Book of Job, and the word now means anything enormous.

clue.text: Loud English pub hustled pair off

indicators.note: things hustled are pushed and jostled roughly, so the letters are knocked about

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy English pub where people are jostled into couples.
explanation.definitionFit: To double up is to form twos or share with a partner, which is splitting into couples.

clue.text: Dislike a translation

blocks.note: taken as written
a translation of a text is a version of it

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a particular translation.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong distaste or antipathy towards something, so it is a noun for not liking.

clue.text: Outlaw skirts humble dwelling in Himalayan kingdom

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so the first word surrounds the second

blocks.note: to outlaw is to ban
a hut is a simple, modest home

explanation.surface: A fugitive hides near a mountain shack in the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a person who skirts a hut, but it is the verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhutan is a small mountainous monarchy in the eastern Himalayas, between India and China.

clue.text: No more than half the air temperature

indicators.note: half means only the front five of the ten letters are kept, the rest discarded

blocks.note: the atmosphere is the air around the earth
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A weather reading quoting only part of the air temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: At most sets an upper limit, meaning not exceeding a stated amount, which is a ceiling or maximum.

clue.text: I sit in the box I built and I show off

definitions.note: the clue speaks as the person, so 'I' stands for the noun

indicators.note: something built is put together from parts, so these letters are assembled into a fresh order

blocks.clueFragment: I sit in the box I
blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A proud showman sits inside a box of their own construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I built' looks like plain past tense, but built is the anagram signal on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibitionist is someone who craves attention and makes a display of themselves, as the speaker does.

clue.text: One traveller from the east seen in portrait

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a mage is one of the Magi, the wise men from the East in the Nativity story

explanation.surface: One of the Three Wise Men appears in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' sounds like a container signal, but here it simply joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or picture of someone, which is exactly what a painted portrait is.

clue.text: On the predecessors of Q

blocks.note: first meaning: placed upon
second meaning: the alphabet letters running A to P, all of which come before Q

explanation.walkthrough: Read as A TO P, the answer is the run of letters preceding Q in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of, so an object resting upon something else is sitting on it.

clue.text: Decay in support for administrator

indicators.note: in says one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: rust is corrosion, a form of decay
a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Something rotting inside a structural prop is a worry for whoever manages it.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf tee is the small peg the ball rests on before the drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee manages property or funds held on behalf of others, so is an administrator of a trust.

clue.text: I start to go in - or am I folding?

indicators.note: the start of the following word is its opening letter alone
in tells you the first two pieces go inside the closing phrase

blocks.note: taken as written
opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are going in or giving up, folding like a poker player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folding' reads as the poker sense of quitting, which makes 'go in' feel like betting.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of creasing paper into shapes, so it is the craft of folding.

clue.text: Caribbean stew for Spooner's philosopher doggie, perhaps

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

blocks.note: Karl Popper the philosopher of science, and a pet, of which a doggie is one example; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A philosopher's dog suggests a Caribbean dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner swaps the sounds after the shared P, so the vowels change places between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperpot is a spiced meat stew from the West Indies, especially Guyana, made with cassareep.

clue.text: Cor anglais finally beginning to entertain ninnies

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows
the beginning of the following word is its opening letter

blocks.note: both are exclamations of surprise
closing letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: A cor anglais, the woodwind instrument, starts to amuse some fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor anglais' looks like the oboe-family instrument, but Cor is the British exclamation of surprise, like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling people geese is an old way of saying they are silly or foolish, so they are simpletons.
